_comment: Publisher-stated permission-to-quote limits for the nine modern, actively copyrighted translations in models.schemas.BIBLE_TRANSLATIONS (KJV and Douay-Rheims are public domain and deliberately not listed here -- see PUBLIC_DOMAIN_BIBLE_TRANSLATIONS). Sourced directly from each publisher's own permissions/copyright page via WebSearch, cross-checked against at least one independent secondary source per entry (studylight.org's Copyright Statements collection, which mirrors publisher-supplied notices verbatim) where the primary page could not be fetched directly. This is metadata about a LICENSING POLICY, never the translations' own copyrighted text -- same 'never store copyrighted text' rule docs/CONTENT_CONTRIBUTING.md states for every other curated content file in this repo. These limits are far beyond anything Bede's own ordinary tutoring (a verse or two per turn, never a stored or reprinted passage) would ever approach; they're recorded here for completeness and parent transparency, not because Bede's actual usage is expected to test them. The operative constraint on Bede's own Scripture quoting stays ACCURACY, not these limits -- see services/ai_service.py's _bible_translation_note: Bede has no verified, licensed copy of any of these texts to check itself against, so its own memorized wording for a specific translation may not be exact, independent of how generous that publisher's own license actually is.

ESV.conditions: not more than half of any one Bible book, nor 25% or more of the quoting work; not permitted in a commentary or other biblical reference work

NIV.conditions: not a complete Bible book, nor 25% or more of the quoting work; not permitted in a commentary or other biblical reference work

NASB.conditions: not a complete Bible book, nor 50% or more of the quoting work

NLT.conditions: not a complete Bible book, nor 25% or more of the quoting work

CSB.conditions: not a complete Bible book, nor 50% or more of the quoting work

NKJV.conditions: not a complete Bible book, nor 25% or more of the quoting work
NKJV.notes: Secondary sources disagree here -- some report a 1,000-verse/50% threshold instead. The two could not be reconciled against a single primary source, so the more conservative, more consistently cited figure is used.

RSV-CE.conditions: not a complete Bible book, nor 50% or more of the quoting work

NRSV-CE.conditions: not a complete Bible book, nor 50% or more of the quoting work
NRSV-CE.notes: NRSV-CE follows the same NRSV permissions policy -- the Catholic Edition is the same base translation with the deuterocanonical books included/reordered, not a separately licensed text.

NABRE.conditions: not more than 40% of a single Bible book, nor 40% or more of the quoting work
NABRE.notes: This publisher states its threshold in WORDS, not verses, unlike every other entry here -- kept as its own field (free_quote_words) rather than estimated into a verse count.
